text.headline: Bitcoin weakens as fund withdrawals continue
text.tone: Confirmed reports of significant fund withdrawals and regulatory concerns weighed on digital assets, though the broader market remains sensitive to shifting risk appetites.
lead: Bitcoin fell 4.3% on Tuesday, marking a sharp decline on the [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]] page. This move coincided with a 1.2% retreat in US large caps and a drop in the VIX volatility index in the latest data.

The decline in digital assets is consistent with confirmed reports of deepening outflows from exchange-traded funds, including a $6.8 million sale by a major fund manager. Bitcoin fell alongside equities, behaving like a risk asset rather than a safe haven. This pattern suggests that crypto demand is currently sensitive to broader financial market sentiment.

Industrial metals also faced pressure, as copper fell 1.1% on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]]. The simultaneous retreat of platinum and copper may reflect softer expectations for industrial and automotive demand. The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] notes that world stocks are currently trading below their 200-day average.

Future sessions will clarify if this crypto retreat persists as ETF outflows approach $5 billion for the month. A stabilization in digital assets would weaken the current regulatory and flow-based interpretation, while further equity declines could confirm a broader risk-off regime.

briefs.markets: US large caps fell 1.2% on Tuesday, while the US 10-year yield dropped 12 basis points in the latest data on the [[markets|Financial Markets]].
briefs.energy: Brent crude was last recorded at $92.94 on the [[energy|Energy Terminal]], as markets monitor geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Ukraine.
briefs.crypto: Bitcoin dropped 4.3% amid reports of $4.9 billion in monthly ETF outflows on the [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]] page.
briefs.metals: Copper and silver declined on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]], a move consistent with weaker industrial demand expectations.
briefs.estate: The [[estate|Estate Index]] shows divergent global trends, with house prices falling 6.3% in China while rising 26.7% in Türkiye.
briefs.corporate: The [[corporate|Corporate Monitor]] identifies APA Corporation as a top-scoring firm during a week characterized by a risk-off market regime.
briefs.outlook: The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] highlights significant quarterly declines in semiconductors and artificial intelligence themes as growth worries persist.
briefs.islamic: The EB Shariah US 100 fell 1.3% on Tuesday, though it maintains a 7.7% year-to-date gain on the [[islamic|Islamic Investment]] page.

watch: US–China trade news involving potential 20% tariffs, which has seen high news volume but has not yet triggered a confirmed reaction in broader equity markets.
Taiwan Strait security developments, as increased news coverage regarding regional integration and military updates could eventually influence semiconductor and technology sector volatility.
The US 10-year yield, which fell to 4.92% in recent data; further declines would strengthen the interpretation that markets are pricing in slower economic growth.
